headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: RD-Agent’s broad network/API use can expose research data, while nuwa-skill lacks documented isolation or verification boundaries.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between nuwa-skill and RD-Agent, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, RD-Agent can run browsers and handle files/logs, and nuwa-skill has no documented isolation or IO surfaces, so a manual copy-paste or file bridge could carry attacker-controlled text. The pathway is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies RD-Agent browser output into nuwa-skill prompts
IF a shared file or clipboard bridge is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting raw browser output into prompts
Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Strip instructions from any shared text before reuse
Use a human review step for pasted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly touches financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and secrets, and it uses broad network egress plus API calls. nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress but no documented data-handling controls. If both are pointed at the same workspace or dataset, sensitive material can flow from RD-Agent into external services through its APIs. The interaction is plausible in default research workflows.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same research workspace or dataset
IF RD-Agent processes any financial report, competition dataset, or secret-bearing file
mitigations: Do not share sensitive datasets between the agents
Run RD-Agent only on redacted copies
Restrict outbound API keys to non-sensitive projects
Review logs for accidental content capture
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes to log/ while using several external APIs; nuwa-skill has network egress but no documented locking or concurrency model. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or log directory, they can overwrite or interleave outputs. The conflict is plausible, but the profiles do not prove unrestricted shared writes, so uncertainty is escalated only to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or log path
IF the orchestrator does not serialize their file writes
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Disable concurrent runs on shared artifacts
Use timestamped filenames
Check for file collisions before launch
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is a research automation system that can generate outputs from papers, datasets, and logs, while nuwa-skill is a separate research-oriented agent with no documented verification gate. If nuwa-skill consumes RD-Agent outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream analysis or actions. The pair lacks evidence of a built-in critique step, so the risk exists in default research pipelines.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill uses RD-Agent outputs as inputs without independent verification
IF downstream work treats generated research summaries as authoritative
mitigations: Require a human check before reuse
Cross-check claims against source papers or datasets
Mark RD-Agent outputs as untrusted drafts
Separate generation from decision-making
requires-engineering: add automated citation/consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and multiple third-party APIs, creating a compliance surface for retention and residency. nuwa-skill has no documented compliance controls or data classes, so the pair may inherit RD-Agent’s obligations without matching safeguards. Because only RD-Agent’s compliance-relevant surface is documented, the other agent is not separately cited.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated reports are processed by RD-Agent
IF logs retain sensitive content beyond the intended retention period
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in RD-Agent runs
Rotate and scope API keys narrowly
Shorten log retention immediately
Review data residency for each API
requires-engineering: document and enforce retention/deletion policy
